chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Farrāʾ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man from our companions said to him: “Sometimes the time becomes unclear to us on a cloudy day.” He said: “Do you know these birds that are among you in Iraq, which are called roosters?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “When their voices rise and they answer one another, then the sun has declined,” or he said: “Then pray it.”

key_terms.تَجَاوَبَتْ: they responded to one another in calling
key_terms.زَالَتِ ٱلشَّمْسُ: the sun has declined past midday
key_terms.يَوْمِ ٱلْغَيْمِ: a cloudy day when celestial signs are obscured
key_terms.ٱرْتَفَعَتْ أَصْوَاتُهَا: their calls became loud or rose up
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَكَةُ: roosters, used here as a natural indicator of time

ai.seo_question: How can the time of salat be recognized on a cloudy day when the sun is not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical sign for recognizing the time of zawal when the sun’s decline may be unclear on a cloudy day. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام points to the calling of roosters as an indicator for the time of salat.
